newsitem.title: JAPAN: Top Japan breweries show contrasting 6-mth results.
newsitem.headline: Top Japan breweries show contrasting 6-mth results.

text.p: Strong beer sales put the fizz in Asahi Breweries Ltd's earnings in the first half of the year while its rival, Kirin Brewery Co Ltd, came up short.

Asahi Breweries, the country's second largest beer producer, said on Tuesday that its parent current profit reached 18.17 billion yen ($155 million) in the first six months, up 44.9 percent from the same period a year ago.
"The profit rise is mainly because of robust sales of our beer," said an Asahi spokesman.
Current profit is pretax profit and includes gains and losses from non-operating activities.
While Asahi enjoyed strong sales of its mainstay brand, Super Dry, which was the best selling beer for the half-year period, industry leader Kirin Brewery's earnings fell.
Kirin said on Monday that its parent current profit declined to 25.25 billion yen ($215 million) from 27.53 billion yen ($235 million) a year ago.
Asahi said shipments of Super Dry in the January-June period jumped 20 percent from a year ago to a total of 955,197 kilolitres.
Meanwhile, shipments of Kirin's mainstay Kirin Lager fell 11.7 percent from a year ago to 801,378 kilolitres.
Analysts pointed out that Super Dry's success was partly due to Asahi's emphasis on marketing the product to supermarkets and mass retailers rather than small liquor shops.
Encouraged by booming sales, Asahi president Yuzo Seto told Reuters last month that the company expects its share in the domestic beer market to rise to 35 percent by the end of this year.
Asahi captured 30.4 percent of the market in 1996, up 3.2 percentage points from a year ago, while Kirin's share declined 2.3 percentage points from the previous year to 46.6 percent.
However, Asahi's earnings outlook is not without worries.

In the second half of 1997, Asahi will have to write off losses totalling about 18 billion yen ($153 million) from previous investments in financial markets as it could not write off part of the losses in the first half, an Asahi spokesman said.
The write-off was postponed because Asahi had to write off separate losses of eight billion yen ($68.3 million) stemming from its investment in Australian beer maker Foster's Brewing Group Ltd.
Asahi said earlier this week that it expects a loss of A$216.24 million from its sale of Foster shares held by its wholly owned Australian subsidiary. Asahi has already written off the expected loss.
Nevertheless, the Asahi spokesman said that the company maintains its forecast of posting a parent current profit of 35 billion yen ($299 million) in the year to December 31, 1997.
"Our beer sales are strong enough to cover the negative impact of the non-operational loss," he said. ($1=117 yen)
